extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, parties in PTAB/IP appeals, and patent applicants
extracted.subtask_short: PTAB appeal: provisional as prior art
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts legal standards for when an unpublished provisional application becomes prior art through incorporation by reference into a published PCT application, and related procedural and review rules in PTAB/IPR appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printed publication (35 U.S.C. §102) — public availability test
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'printed publication' under the applicable version of § 102(b) must have been publicly available at the pertinent time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: That requirement is met if the document was 'disseminated or otherwise made available to the extent that persons interested and ordinarily skilled in the subject matter or art exercising reasonable diligence, [could have] locate[d] it.' (Kyocera Wireless Corp. v. Int’l. Trade Comm’n, 545 F.3d 1340, 1350 (Fed. Cir. 2008), quoting SRI Int’l, Inc. v. Internet Security Systems, Inc., 511 F.3d 1186, 1194 (Fed. Cir. 2008)). The inquiry is whether the document was accessible such that those skilled in the art exercising reasonable diligence could find it.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 1.14(a)(1)(vi) — access to 'application as originally filed' when incorporated in published PCT
rubrics_metrics.description: Under § 1.14(a)(1)(vi), 'A copy of the application as originally filed of an unpublished pending application may be provided to any person, upon written request and payment of the appropriate fee... if the application is incorporated by reference or otherwise identified in ... an international publication of an international application under PCT Article 21(2).'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulation distinguishes between the 'application as originally filed' (which may be provided in the incorporation-by-reference/PCT-publication circumstance) and the 'paper file' or file history (for which separate access rules apply). The Board interpreted this to mean the incorporated provisional 'as originally filed' becomes accessible without the inventor's written authorization when published in a PCT that incorporates it by reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 1.14 — distinction between 'paper file' and 'application as originally filed' (authorization requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will not provide access to the paper file of a pending application, except as provided in paragraph (c) or (i) of this section; paragraph (c) requires written authorization by the inventor or other authorized person for access to a pending application's paper file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This limitation on access to the paper file does not preclude provision of the 'application as originally filed' where § 1.14(a)(1)(vi) applies (incorporation by reference in a published international application). Thus, even if the file history remains confidential absent authorization, the 'application as originally filed' may nonetheless become publicly accessible under the incorporation-by-reference exception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of incorporation by reference in a published PCT
rubrics_metrics.description: When a published PCT expressly incorporates the entirety of an earlier provisional application by reference, the incorporated provisional 'became publicly available as of the date the [PCT] published.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequently, the provisional can be treated as prior art both 'by virtue of the fact that it became publicly available due to its incorporation into' the published PCT, and 'in addition... as part of the' PCT publication itself. The Board applied this principle to find the provisional anticipatory/prior art against challenged claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: MPEP guidance is persuasive but not law
rubrics_metrics.description: The Manual of Patent Examining Procedure (MPEP) 'does not have the force of law.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nonetheless, the MPEP may explain how regulations operate (e.g., MPEP § 103(III) explaining that incorporation by reference in a published international application constitutes special circumstances warranting provision of a copy of the application-as-filed upon request). MPEP can support the Board's interpretation of a regulation, but it cannot override statutory or regulatory text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority/effective filing date under 35 U.S.C. §120 — sufficiency of support
rubrics_metrics.description: To claim priority under § 120 to earlier filings (e.g., a PCT or provisional), the claims must be sufficiently supported by those earlier filings; otherwise the claim's effective filing date may be the later filed national application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The effective filing date determination controls what constitutes prior art for the claims at issue; if the chain of priority 'could not reach back further under 35 U.S.C. § 120' because claims lacked sufficient support, earlier provisional/PCT filings cannot serve as the patent's effective date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard of review in PTAB appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: The court reviews the Board's legal conclusions de novo and its factual determinations for substantial-evidence support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether an asserted anticipatory document qualifies as a 'printed publication' under § 102 is a legal conclusion based on underlying factual determinations (In re Lister, 583 F.3d 1307, 1311 (Fed. Cir. 2009)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Forfeiture of issues raised first on rehearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Arguments raised for the first time on rehearing to the Board are forfeited under the governing procedural rules (37 C.F.R. § 42.71(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A party cannot rely on evidence or assertions first presented on rehearing to reverse or alter the Board's decision unless preserved earlier in the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interplay of 35 U.S.C. §122 confidentiality and regulatory exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: While 35 U.S.C. § 122 generally addresses confidentiality of pending applications, regulations (37 C.F.R. § 1.14(a)(1)(vi)) and MPEP interpretation delineate specific exceptions (such as incorporation into a published international application) that permit public access to the application-as-filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A party must show that a regulation is unauthorized or contrary to statute to prevail against the Board's regulatory-based access determination; mere invocation of § 122's confidentiality without challenging the regulation's validity is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical consequence rule: incorporated provisional can be used in unpatentability arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: If a provisional application becomes publicly available through incorporation in a PCT publication, it may be relied upon as prior art to support unpatentability arguments (anticipation or obviousness) against later-filed claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board may treat the provisional both as the source of disclosed limitations and as part of the published PCT itself when evaluating anticipation/obviousness; the effective-date/prior-art analysis follows from the public-availability and incorporation determinations.
